data.body_html:
Imagine a morning on the Mediterranean, cava in hand, as dolphins arc through the turquoise water off Marbella. The Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2027 combines the thrill of spotting wild dolphins with a relaxed brunch on a private yacht. Departing from Puerto Banús, this experience is perfect for families, couples, or small groups looking for a unique start to the day. With our fleet of motor yachts and catamarans, you can choose the perfect vessel for your group size and budget.

Why choose a dolphin watching brunch cruise in Marbella?

The Costa del Sol’s Alboran Sea is one of Europe’s best spots for dolphin watching, with sightings in over 90% of trips. A morning cruise offers calm seas and cooler temperatures, ideal for spotting bottlenose and common dolphins. Adding a brunch with fresh Spanish produce elevates the experience—think ripe mango, jamón serrano, and cava. Unlike crowded tourist boats, our private charters give you a personalised itinerary, a dedicated skipper, and the freedom to linger where dolphins appear.

Our fleet for the 2027 brunch cruise

We offer several vessels for your dolphin watching brunch cruise, all departing from Puerto Banús. For a budget-friendly option, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 passengers) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 passengers) are available from €749 for 2 hours (including skipper, drinks, snacks, and VAT). For a premium experience, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 passengers) starts at €4,719 for 4 hours and includes a free jet ski. Other boats like the Fairline Targa 12m or Lagoon 380 catamaran are available on request—contact us via WhatsApp for pricing.

What’s included in your brunch cruise

  • Licensed English-speaking skipper
  • Fuel for the entire journey
  • Brunch: fresh fruit, pastries, Spanish omelette, artisan bread, and cava
  • Unlimited water, soft drinks, beer, and white wine
  • Light snacks (olives, nuts, chips)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

On longer charters (4+ hours), you can also enjoy a swim stop at Cala Cortés or Cabopino beach.

Typical itinerary for a 2-hour morning cruise

Your cruise departs Puerto Banús at 10:00 or 11:00. The skipper heads southwest toward Cabopino, where dolphins often feed. Within 20–30 minutes, you’re likely to spot pods swimming alongside the boat. The brunch is served as you drift, with cava and music setting the mood. After about 90 minutes, you’ll return along the coast, passing the Golden Mile and Marbella’s skyline. The total time on the water is 2 hours, but you can extend to 4 or 8 hours for a more leisurely pace.

Best time for dolphin watching in Marbella

Dolphins are present year-round, but the best visibility and sea conditions are from May to October, when water temperatures range from 22°C to 30°C. Mornings (10:00–12:00) are optimal because the sea is calmer, and dolphins are more active after feeding. July and August are peak season, so book at least a week in advance. Our skippers monitor local dolphin movements daily to maximise your chances.
